subject: general
question: A certain number of people are sitting in a straight row, facing north. B is fourth to the left of G; F is fourth to the right of C and second to the left of K, who is fifth to the right of A. D is not an immediate neighbour of either K or B. There are only three persons between J and A. J and K are sitting at extreme ends. G is second to the right of C. If no other person is sitting in the row, What is the total number of persons seated?
solution:
Given: A certain number of people are sitting in a straight row, facing north.

1) F is fourth to the right of C and second to the left of K, who is fifth to the right of A.

2) There are only three persons between J and A.

3) G is second to the right of C. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07845122212623b4c2452aaec8899d71ecb24d7ad639737188bf4e00e033febb.png] 

4) B is fourth to the left of G.

5) D is not an immediate neighbour of either K or B.

6) J and K are sitting at extreme ends. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ef739644e7ed0d5b682ce6197397987008fa36a4c0232a0569bc8479fa72275.png] 

So, If no other person is sitting in the row, then total 'Ten' persons are seated in the row.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.
